framework: UNESCO Global MIL & SIFT Lateral Reading

fallacies.name: Ad Hominem
fallacies.subtitle: Character Smear & Deflection
fallacies.description: Attacking an opponent's character, personality, or background rather than engaging with the substantive empirical merits of their argument.
fallacies.psychology: Exploits out-group tribal hostility and moral disgust to bypass analytical evaluation of factual evidence.
fallacies.viral_example: "Don't listen to Dr. Aris's peer-reviewed climate data—he was once paid by a consulting firm so he is obviously a corrupt shill!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: If you strip away the personal insults, what actual empirical data or evidence remains in the claim?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Evaluation & Ethical Assessment
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace the primary data independent of the spokesperson's personality.

fallacies.name: False Dilemma
fallacies.subtitle: Forced Black-and-White Dichotomy
fallacies.description: Artificially reducing a complex, multi-variable reality into only two extreme, mutually exclusive options while erasing all nuanced middle grounds.
fallacies.psychology: Leverages cognitive simplicity bias—the brain's tendency to prefer binary categories over exhausting nuance during stress.
fallacies.viral_example: "Either you 100% support this controversial surveillance bill, or you want terrorists to attack our schools!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: What third, fourth, or compromise alternatives are being intentionally excluded by this ultimatum?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Critical Analysis of Media Content
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage across independent spectrums.

fallacies.name: Appeal to Fear
fallacies.subtitle: Catastrophizing & Doomsday Bait
fallacies.description: Using terrifying, apocalyptic predictions to trigger an instinctual fight-or-flight response, forcing compliance without verification.
fallacies.psychology: Activates the amygdala and suppresses prefrontal cortex rational scrutiny through acute perceived threat.
fallacies.viral_example: "If this treaty passes tomorrow, our society will face irreversible total annihilation and economic ruin within weeks!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Does the underlying scientific consensus actually predict this catastrophic timeline, or is terror being used as persuasion?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Critical Engagement & Cognitive Autonomy
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Pause when feeling a surge of acute existential dread.

fallacies.name: Confirmation Bias
fallacies.subtitle: Echo Chamber Validation
fallacies.description: The subconscious tendency to eagerly accept and share information that confirms existing prejudices while aggressively rationalizing away contrary proof.
fallacies.psychology: Protects ego identity and social standing within an ideological tribe by avoiding cognitive dissonance.
fallacies.viral_example: "I knew the opposing party was secretly running that ring! I won't even check if this screenshot is photoshopped because it feels so true."
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Would I scrutinize this claim more aggressively if it attacked a public figure I admire?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Metacognition & Self-Reflection
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate the Source from counter-perspective wire services.

fallacies.name: Weasel Words
fallacies.subtitle: Vague & Passive Attribution
fallacies.description: Creating the illusion of widespread authoritative backing through anonymous, nebulous phrasing ('experts warn', 'many people are saying').
fallacies.psychology: Exploits conformity and authority bias without accepting the legal or journalistic liability of naming specific researchers.
fallacies.viral_example: "Leading scientists all agree without a doubt that this secret household spice eliminates 100% of toxins!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Which specific university, medical institution, or published paper is actually named in the body text?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 2: Verification of Information Sources
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace Claim: Locate the original peer-reviewed publication.

fallacies.name: Artificial Urgency
fallacies.subtitle: Scam Pressure & Panic Trap
fallacies.description: Imposing artificial deadlines ('Act now in 15 minutes or your account will be deleted') to short-circuit analytical reasoning.
fallacies.psychology: Uses fear of loss (loss aversion) and hyper-arousal to make the victim act impulsively before consulting trusted peers.
fallacies.viral_example: "URGENT SECURITY ALERT: Your crypto wallet has been compromised. Verify your secret seed phrase within 10 minutes or lose all funds!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Why is this platform demanding instant action rather than allowing me to navigate directly through their official app?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Digital Safety & Scam Resistance
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Never click links inside urgent SMS, email, or DMs.

fallacies.name: Strawman Argument
fallacies.subtitle: Caricaturing & Distorting Claims
fallacies.description: Misrepresenting an opponent's nuanced argument into an absurd, extreme caricature that is ridiculously easy to knock down.
fallacies.psychology: Simplifies complex policy debates into cheap emotional victories for partisan audiences.
fallacies.viral_example: "Proponents of school lunch subsidies want to replace all parental authority with totalitarian state kitchen inspectors!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Did the original advocates actually propose that extreme policy, or did the critic invent that scenario?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Critical Analysis of Discourse
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace the original quote in its complete, unedited context.

fallacies.name: Bandwagon Effect
fallacies.subtitle: Social Proof Manipulation
fallacies.description: Arguing that a claim must be valid or high-quality simply because millions of people believe it or it has 10M views on TikTok.
fallacies.psychology: Exploits evolutionary herd instincts where individual safety was historically linked to following the majority consensus.
fallacies.viral_example: "Over 5 million people bought this miracle magnetic detox bracelet this week—it can't possibly be fake!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Can millions of well-intentioned people be swayed by viral marketing or algorithmic momentum without empirical evidence?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Differentiating Virality from Veracity
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate whether independent consumer protection agencies verified the claim.

fallacies.name: Sunk Cost Bias
fallacies.subtitle: Entrenched Commitment Trap
fallacies.description: Refusing to abandon a discredited belief, investment, or political figure because of the enormous time, money, or reputation already invested in it.
fallacies.psychology: Driven by intense aversion to admitting personal error and public loss of status.
fallacies.viral_example: "I've already invested $5,000 into this trading scheme and defended it to all my friends. I have to put in another $2,000 to prove I was right!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: If I was discovering this situation with fresh eyes today with zero prior investment, what decision would I make?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Ethical & Reflective Information Processing
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Seek dispassionate third-party financial or academic counsel.

fallacies.name: Halo Effect
fallacies.subtitle: Celebrity & Influencer Overreach
fallacies.description: Assuming that a person's charisma, athletic skill, or celebrity status in one domain gives them authoritative expertise on complex unrelated subjects.
fallacies.psychology: Our brains generalize a positive impression in one visible area to all unseen cognitive domains.
fallacies.viral_example: "My favorite pop singer posted that drinking raw volcanic ash cures viral infections, so it must be medically sound!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: What peer-reviewed biomedical qualifications does this entertainer or sports star hold in immunology?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 2: Verifying Domain-Specific Authority
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate Source: Check medical consensus on WHO, CDC, or PubMed.

fallacies.name: Cherry Picking
fallacies.subtitle: Suppressed Evidence & Selective Data
fallacies.description: Carefully selecting isolated data points or outliers that support a preferred narrative while deliberately hiding the overwhelming majority of contrary data.
fallacies.psychology: Creates the false illusion of empirical statistical backing while misleading through omission.
fallacies.viral_example: "Global warming is a total hoax! Look at this single town in Siberia that had a record cold night last Thursday!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Does this isolated anecdote represent the global 50-year aggregate trend, or is it a selective outlier?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Statistical & Scientific Literacy
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage: Consult NASA, IPCC, or meteorological aggregate reports.

fallacies.name: Conspiracy Framing
fallacies.subtitle: The Suppression Myth
fallacies.description: Claiming that the total absence of verifiable evidence for a theory is actually definitive proof of a massive institutional cover-up.
fallacies.psychology: Provides an unfalsifiable psychological shield—every debunking attempt is re-interpreted as part of the conspiracy itself.
fallacies.viral_example: "Mainstream media won't report this secret cure because Big Pharma pays billions to keep humanity sick! Share before deleted!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Is this hypothesis constructed so that no amount of counter-evidence can ever disprove it in the author's eyes?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Dissecting Epistemic Bubbles & Conspiracies
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace the origin of the suppression claim using Google Fact Check.

fallacies.name: Slippery Slope
fallacies.subtitle: The Domino Fallacy & Inevitable Catastrophe
fallacies.description: Asserting that a minor initial step or moderate policy will inevitably trigger a catastrophic, extreme chain of events without demonstrating any proven causal link.
fallacies.psychology: Exploits catastrophizing heuristics and the brain's difficulty in evaluating compounding conditional probabilities across multi-step scenarios.
fallacies.viral_example: "If the city approves this 15-minute neighborhood zoning pilot, the next step will be mandatory movement permits, digital ration cards, and the complete confiscation of private vehicles!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Has the author demonstrated an unbroken, evidence-backed causal chain between the first step and the final disaster, or are they ignoring multiple intermediate safeguards and democratic checkpoints?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Critical Analysis of Causal Chains
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage: Consult independent urban planning and legislative analyses to verify whether similar policies historically produced the claimed domino effect.

fallacies.name: Whataboutism
fallacies.subtitle: Hypocrisy Deflection & Tu Quoque
fallacies.description: Deflecting legitimate criticism or factual allegations by immediately pointing to an unrelated wrongdoing or inconsistency committed by an opponent.
fallacies.psychology: Triggers moral outrage and tribal defensiveness, shifting cognitive focus away from evaluating the immediate accusation to relitigating unrelated historical grievances.
fallacies.viral_example: "Why is the media investigating our company's unauthorized data harvesting? What about when that foreign tech giant leaked 100 million user records three years ago and faced zero penalties?!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Does highlighting another party's past misconduct resolve, disprove, or answer the specific evidence behind the current allegation?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Dialectical Integrity & Accountability
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Refocus on verifying the primary claim before allowing the dialogue to be derailed by secondary comparisons.

fallacies.name: False Cause
fallacies.subtitle: Post Hoc & Spurious Correlation
fallacies.description: Assuming that because Event B occurred after or alongside Event A, Event A must have directly caused Event B, confusing coincidence or correlation with genuine causation.
fallacies.psychology: Leverages teleological thinking and evolutionary patternicity—the instinctual human drive to infer direct causal intent from chronological sequence.
fallacies.viral_example: "Local clinic visits spiked right after the new telecommunications tower was activated last month, proving that radio frequencies are destroying neighborhood immune systems!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Did Event A cause Event B through a verified scientific mechanism, or did they simply coincide due to seasonal shifts, third-variable confounders, or pure chance?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Scientific & Empirical Reasoning
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace Claim: Query epidemiological and peer-reviewed databases (e.g. PubMed, Cochrane) to verify established causal mechanisms.

fallacies.name: False Authority
fallacies.subtitle: Irrelevant Credential Overreach
fallacies.description: Citing an individual with formal credentials in one specialized field to substantiate authoritative claims in a completely unrelated, complex discipline.
fallacies.psychology: Exploits credential deference—audiences see a formal title ('Doctor', 'Professor', 'Engineer') and automatically assume universal domain competence across all sciences.
fallacies.viral_example: "A world-renowned aerospace engineering professor just published a blog post claiming that dietary cholesterol does not affect cardiac health—who are you going to trust, a literal rocket scientist or mainstream dietitians?!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Is this expert's formal academic training, published research history, and peer-reviewed track record specifically in the discipline they are making claims about?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 2: Verification of Domain-Specific Authority
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate the Source: Conduct a lateral search of the author's primary publication record on Google Scholar and institutional faculty directories.

fallacies.name: Appeal to Nature
fallacies.subtitle: Naturalistic Health Fallacy
fallacies.description: Arguing that a product or treatment is inherently safe, beneficial, and effective because it is 'natural', while asserting that anything synthetic or laboratory-refined is toxic.
fallacies.psychology: Activates purity heuristics and naturalistic essentialism, pairing evolutionary disgust toward artificial adulteration with a romanticized ideal of untouched nature.
fallacies.viral_example: "Throw away your laboratory blood pressure prescriptions! This wild-harvested jungle root is 100% all-natural, meaning it has zero side effects and completely cures cardiovascular disease!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Are natural substances (such as arsenic, hemlock, or snake venom) inherently safe, and are laboratory-formulated compounds inherently dangerous without empirical clinical trial data?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Biomedical & Chemical Literacy
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace Claim: Check clinical toxicology registers and public health bodies (WHO, FDA, EMA) for peer-reviewed efficacy and toxicity trials.

fallacies.name: No True Scotsman
fallacies.subtitle: The Purity Shield & Shifting Definitions
fallacies.description: Protecting a universal claim from clear counterexamples by retroactively altering the definition of the group to exclude the inconvenient case.
fallacies.psychology: Provides cognitive immunization, enabling individuals to protect cherished dogmas and group identity from falsification and cognitive dissonance.
fallacies.viral_example: "Real journalists would never publish stories critical of our movement. If a reporter wrote that investigative article, they were never a genuine, ethical journalist in the first place!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Did the speaker arbitrarily redefine the boundaries or criteria of the group solely to dismiss a legitimate counterexample that disproved their original generalization?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 3: Critical Evaluation of Ideological Claims
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage: Consult established, independent professional standards and academic definitions from diverse reputable organizations.

fallacies.name: Anchoring Bias
fallacies.subtitle: First Number Fixation & Price Priming
fallacies.description: Fixating disproportionately on the first piece of numerical information encountered, allowing that initial anchor to distort subsequent value judgments, estimates, and negotiations.
fallacies.psychology: Driven by the anchoring-and-adjustment heuristic, where the human brain insufficiently adjusts away from an arbitrary initial figure when assessing real worth under uncertainty.
fallacies.viral_example: "This algorithmic crypto trading course is valued at $10,000 by Wall Street insiders, but for the next 2 hours you can access it for only $97! Save $9,903 instantly!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Is the initial reference price a verified, market-tested baseline, or is it an artificial anchor created to make the secondary price seem like an irresistible discount?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Financial Literacy & Cognitive Autonomy
fallacies.sift_strategy: Investigate the Source: Lateral search independent price-tracking engines and open-market competitors to determine genuine baseline valuations.

fallacies.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
fallacies.subtitle: Overconfidence Bias & Novice Blindness
fallacies.description: A cognitive blindspot wherein individuals with minimal knowledge or superficial exposure to a complex subject vastly overestimate their own expertise and dismiss domain specialists.
fallacies.psychology: A dual-burden metacognitive deficit—the absence of deep knowledge in a domain simultaneously deprives the novice of the ability to evaluate their own incompetence accurately.
fallacies.viral_example: "I watched three video essays over the weekend and now I understand national monetary policy and currency inflation far better than career central bank economists!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Do I possess the methodological training and domain depth necessary to dismiss the consensus of career researchers after brief, informal media consumption?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 5: Metacognitive Humility & Self-Assessment
fallacies.sift_strategy: Stop: Acknowledge personal knowledge boundaries and cross-reference foundational university textbooks or comprehensive academic literature reviews.

fallacies.name: Hasty Generalization
fallacies.subtitle: Anecdotal Extrapolation & Micro-Sample Bias
fallacies.description: Drawing broad, universal conclusions about an entire population, demographic, or technology based on an isolated anecdote or statistically inadequate sample size.
fallacies.psychology: Driven by base-rate neglect and the availability heuristic—vivid, emotionally compelling stories are recalled with ease, leading the brain to substitute individual cases for aggregate probability.
fallacies.viral_example: "My cousin bought an electric vehicle and the battery died in subzero weather during his first road trip. Electric vehicles are a completely unviable scam that will never work for anyone!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Is this viral video or personal story representative of aggregate real-world performance, or am I extrapolating a universal truth from a sample size of one?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Statistical Sampling & Empirical Validity
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage: Search for large-scale fleet telemetry, aggregate consumer reports, and statistically robust cohort studies.

fallacies.name: Circular Reasoning
fallacies.subtitle: Begging the Question & Tautological Loops
fallacies.description: Constructing an argument whose conclusion is presupposed directly in the premises, offering a self-referential loop rather than external empirical evidence.
fallacies.psychology: Leverages coherence bias—the brain frequently confuses internal linguistic symmetry and narrative self-consistency with genuine external empirical proof.
fallacies.viral_example: "You can completely trust every leak released by this anonymous account because they only share absolute truth, and we know it is absolute truth because this account posted it!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Does this argument offer independent, third-party corroboration, or is it merely restating its own premise in different words?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 1: Structural Argument & Epistemic Verification
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace Claim: Look for independent primary sources and corroborating documentation outside of the speaker's self-contained narrative loop.

fallacies.name: In-Group Bias
fallacies.subtitle: Tribal Favoritism & Out-Group Devaluation
fallacies.description: Evaluating claims, actions, and ethics through tribal allegiance, generously forgiving questionable behavior from one's own group while harshly vilifying identical actions from opponents.
fallacies.psychology: Rooted in Social Identity Theory—individuals prioritize social belonging and group status defense over objective factual consistency to avoid social alienation.
fallacies.viral_example: "When our favored political faction uses emergency parliamentary rules, it is bold leadership saving the nation; when the opposing faction does it, it is an unconstitutional coup!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Would I evaluate this exact same statement, policy, or action differently if it were performed by an opponent or a member of an opposing cultural group?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Deconstructing Polarization & Tribalism
fallacies.sift_strategy: Find Better Coverage: Read reporting from non-partisan international wire services and cross-ideological sources to compare rhetorical framing.

fallacies.name: The Liar's Dividend
fallacies.subtitle: Deepfake Cynicism & Accountability Evasion
fallacies.description: Weaponizing public awareness of generative AI and deepfakes to dismiss authentic, verified audio, photographic, or documentary evidence of real-world misconduct as 'synthetic fabrication'.
fallacies.psychology: Induces epistemic nihilism—exploits universal media skepticism to erode the baseline credibility of authentic whistleblowing and journalistic evidence.
fallacies.viral_example: "That leaked audio recording of our campaign manager discussing illicit bribes is a 100% synthetic deepfake created by hostile foreign AI bots! Do not believe what you hear!"
fallacies.reflection_prompt: Is the individual claiming an incriminating piece of evidence is an AI deepfake simply because it exposes their misconduct, without providing verifiable forensic proof of synthesis?
fallacies.mil_competency: UNESCO MIL Law 4: Synthetic Media Literacy & Provenance Verification
fallacies.sift_strategy: Trace to Source: Consult accredited news verification desks and inspect cryptographic metadata (e.g. C2PA provenance credentials) or raw capture records.
